title: The Witness of the Fens Revisited
premise: When the coffin of Fenmarsh's revered founder, Aldous Crane, is exhumed for a tercentenary ceremony and found empty, archivist Sable Oyelaran discovers that the cathedral's locked crypt was opened with a key cut from a pattern hidden in the parish ledgers she has catalogued for years. Following the ledger's cipher, she uncovers a lineage of substitution: three 'accidental' deaths were murders protecting the secret that the town's founding family died out generations ago and its heirs were quietly replaced. The final name in the cipher belongs to Sable herself — her unknown parentage makes her the last true Crane heir, and the killer, the cathedral dean who has guarded the lie his whole life, must silence her before the tercentenary unveiling. In the crypt at dawn, Sable chooses truth over the inheritance and safety the dean offers, exposing him and reclaiming her identity on her own terms.
about_author: Lena Whitlock is the pen name of a former parish records clerk who spent a decade among dusty registers and locked vestries in the English fenlands. She writes mysteries where architecture keeps secrets better than people do.

chapters.title: The Empty Coffin
chapters.summary: Sable Oyelaran oversees preparations to exhume founder Aldous Crane for the tercentenary, dreading the media circus in her quiet archive. When the coffin lid lifts before the mayor and clergy, it holds only river silt and a child's shoe. POV: Sable. Emotional beat: dread curdling into a familiar, unwelcome thrill — she has seen staged deaths here before.

chapters.title: Three Accidents
chapters.summary: Sable privately reviews her own files: a verger's fall, a drowning, a fire, each ruled accidental, each with a ledger discrepancy she never reported. Detective Inspector Harrow arrives and dismisses her theories as archival obsession. POV: Sable, with flashback fragments. Emotional beat: isolation — the cost of being right too many times without proof.

chapters.title: The Ledger in Plain Sight
chapters.summary: Cataloguing the tercentenary display, Sable notices the 1724 parish ledger's marginal flourishes form a repeating cipher keyed to feast days. Decoded entries list names struck through across two centuries — including the three accident victims. POV: Sable. Emotional beat: exhilaration shadowed by fear, because someone else has clearly read this ledger recently; the dust is disturbed.

chapters.title: The Dean's Kindness
chapters.summary: Dean Ambrose Fenn warmly offers Sable a research grant and warns her off 'conspiracy thinking' for her own good. She likes him — he hired her, mentored her. That night someone searches her office but takes nothing. POV: alternating Sable and Harrow. Emotional beat: loyalty under strain; kindness begins to feel like surveillance.

chapters.title: Blood in the Register
chapters.summary: The cipher's struck-through names map onto the Crane family tree — every true-blooded Crane dead by 1900, yet heirs kept appearing. Sable finds a 19th-century adoption record sealed by the dean's own predecessor. POV: Sable. Emotional beat: vertigo of inheritance — the town has been worshipping an empty name for generations.

chapters.title: What the River Kept
chapters.summary: Harrow quietly reopens the drowning case after Sable shows him tide charts proving the body couldn't have drifted as claimed. A witness from the fens recalls seeing the verger alive near the crypt gate. POV: Harrow. Emotional beat: grudging alliance forming between skeptic and archivist, each needing what the other holds.

chapters.title: The Name Beneath Hers
chapters.summary: The cipher's final unstruck entry is a birth record: Oyelaran, mother unnamed, registered by the cathedral itself. Sable confronts the archivist emeritus, who confesses she was brought to Fenmarsh as an infant — a Crane by blood, hidden in plain sight. POV: Sable. Emotional beat: grief and fury; her whole orphaned life was someone's careful arrangement.

chapters.title: Tercentenary Eve
chapters.summary: On the eve of the unveiling, the dean offers Sable everything — legitimacy, the archive, the Crane name — if she lets the past stay buried. She asks for one night to decide. He locks the crypt behind him. POV: Sable. Emotional beat: temptation rendered genuinely seductive; belonging offered at the price of truth.

chapters.title: The Locked Crypt
chapters.summary: Sable decodes the cipher's last instruction — the ledger itself is the founder's confession, meant to be read aloud at the tercentenary — and realizes the dean plans to burn it during the ceremony. She enters the crypt through the flooded fen passage the verger used, finding Aldous Crane's actual remains hidden there. POV: Sable. Emotional beat: terror transmuted into resolve in the dark.

chapters.title: Read Aloud
chapters.summary: At the unveiling, Sable halts the burning of the ledger and reads the founder's confession to the assembled town as Harrow arrests the dean below. She declines the Crane inheritance, keeping only her name and her archive. POV: Sable, closing with Harrow. Emotional beat: quiet triumph — truth chosen over legacy, and an identity finally her own.
